headline: Hungary printed a 100-quintillion-pengő note — the highest-denomination banknote ever issued

sources.title: Guinness World Records — Highest denomination banknote

summary: During Hungary's 1945–46 hyperinflation — the worst on record — the government issued a 100-quintillion-pengő note (1 followed by 20 zeros), printed as "100 million b.-pengő." Guinness World Records lists it as the highest-denomination banknote ever issued (a higher, 1-sextillion-pengő note was printed but never released into circulation). The note is dated 3 June 1946 but didn't actually enter circulation until 11 July 1946, and was withdrawn 31 July 1946 — a real circulation life of about three weeks. Something costing 1 pengő in June 1945 cost 30 septillion pengő by July 1946. In August 1946 Hungary replaced the pengő with the forint at 1 forint = 400 octillion pengő.
